title: Thomas White: IPP review brings 'light' after 14 years in jail

input.lead: Thomas White was jailed 14 years ago on an indeterminate sentence after stealing a mobile phone
input.summary: Thomas White was jailed 14 years ago on an indeterminate sentence after stealing a mobile phone
input.evidence_text: The sister of a man who has been in prison for 14 years without a fixed release date, has welcomed government plans to review "inhumane" indeterminate sentences Thomas White was jailed for a minimum of two years in 2012 for the theft of a mobile phone. He was subject to an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence, with no maximum term and is still serving his sentence But after the Prime Minister asked for a review Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences on Monday , his sister Pastor Clara White said there is now hope in sight "My brother doesn't know if he will ever leave prison or die there," Clara said. "It's inhumane. But the review brings a light in the darkness." Intended for the perpetrators of serious crimes and persistent criminals, Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentences were introduced in 2005. And allowed judges to give out sentences with no maximum tariff to perpetrators of serious crimes or repeat offenders Deemed controversial IPPs were scrapped in 2012, but this was not retrospective. As of this year, more than 2,000 people are still in prison on IPP sentences according to the United Nations, (UN), who have called for the end of IPP sentences. , external

title: Three boys on suspected stolen moped collide with police car

input.lead: Three teenage boys were hospitalised when their stolen moped collided head-on with a police car
input.summary: Three teenage boys were hospitalised when their stolen moped collided head-on with a police car
input.evidence_text: Three boys on suspected stolen moped collide with police car - BBC News Image source, Jonny Humphreys/BBC Image caption, The crash was referred to the Independent Office for Police Conduct Published 1 hour ago Three teenagers were taken to hospital after a suspected stolen moped they were riding collided with a police car. The boys, aged between 14 and 16, were on the moped when it collided with a Greater Manchester Police (GMP) vehicle in Broadoak Park in Wythenshawe, Manchester, at about 15:45 BST on Monday. Two of them remain in hospital for treatment, a GMP spokesman said, adding the force's professional standards department had made a referral to the Independent Office for Police Conduct. title: Warehouse scheme will 'tower over our homes'

input.lead: Families say scaled back plans for homes and "giant" warehouses on farmland will "dwarf" the community
input.summary: Families say scaled back plans for homes and "giant" warehouses on farmland will "dwarf" the community
input.evidence_text: Warehouse scheme will 'tower over our homes' - BBC News Image caption, Amanda Coleman is chairwoman of the Gibfield Preservation Group By Richard Stead North West Published 1 hour ago A campaign group has said that scaled back plans for homes and "giant" warehouses on farmland in Greater Manchester are "still too much" and will "dwarf" the local community. Developer Peel Land has begun a second consultation on plans to build about 500 homes and an industrial estate on farmland between Atherton and Westhoughton. Amanda Coleman, chairwoman of the Gibfield Preservation Group, said: "These are going to be giant warehouses which are going to dwarf and tower over our homes ." Peel Land said: "Careful consideration has been given to the relationship between the new development and existing homes, including a substantial green corridor and planting to screen views." Image caption, The plans include an industrial estate between Gibfield Park Way and Schofield Lane in Atherton Residents have compared the Gibfield Park scheme to the warehouses which were recently built at the Astley Business Park development about four miles away. Coleman, 55, said: "This is going to be metres from the back of our house but its not the distance - its more the height of these warehouses. "They will be built on a hill, so they will be the height of the Astley warehouses." According to the Gibfield Park consultation document, the height of the tallest buildings will be no higher than 12.5 meters (41 ft) and the warehouses will be at least 65 metres from the rear of properties on Schofield Lane. The warehouses in Astley, which were completed by the logistics and industrial property firm PLP in January 2026, reach a height of up to 18 meters. title: Partner of Frankie Jules-Hough opposes killer's early release

input.lead: Calvin Buckley says the man who killed his wife in a car crash shouldn't be eligible for early release
input.summary: Calvin Buckley says the man who killed his wife in a car crash shouldn't be eligible for early release
input.evidence_text: Partner of Frankie Jules-Hough opposes killer's early release - BBC News Image caption, Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough was 38 years old when she was killed by a dangerous driver in 2023 By Georgie Docker North West Published 4 August 2026 A man whose pregnant partner was killed in a 92 mph motorway crash said he is devastated to hear the offender will be eligible for early release from prison. Calvin Buckley's partner Frankie Jules-Hough, a 38-year-old mum-of-two and former Hollyoaks actress, was killed in a crash on the M66 in 2023, by Adil Iqbal. It was earlier confirmed that driving offenders will not be blocked from the early release scheme, which will see thousands of prisoners in England and Wales effectively having their sentences commuted. "I'm devastated," Buckley told BBC Breakfast . "To kill somebody and to have your sentence reduced is just not right. Our justice has been taken away." Iqbal had filmed himself speeding at 123mph before the crash and was jailed for 15 years. "I understand there is a crisis, I agree that it needs to be addressed, but not at the expense of victims," Buckley continued. "Our life was about the children, building a future together. "She was 17 weeks pregnant when she died. "We've had that taken away. "Any offender of that category who has caused catastrophic injuries or death by dangerous driving there is no way they should be up for early release." Image source, Handout Image caption, Frankie was killed on the M66 in Bury, in May 2023, after she had pulled over on the hard shoulder with a tyre puncture Andy Burnham inherited the early release scheme after succeeding Sir Keir Starmer as UK prime minister. Early release scheme: Key facts The early release scheme was introduced after prisons almost reached full capacity

title: Road workers find suspected human remains, closing M67

input.lead: Workers found human remains close to a bridge on the M67 on Tameside on Monday night, police say
input.summary: Workers found human remains close to a bridge on the M67 on Tameside on Monday night, police say
input.evidence_text: Road workers find suspected human remains, closing M67 - BBC News Image caption, Police said the discovery was made close to a bridge between junctions 3 and 4 of the M67 Published 4 August 2026 Suspected human remains have been found by road workers close to a motorway bridge, police have said. Greater Manchester Police said the discovery was made close to a bridge between junctions 3 and 4 of the M67 on Tameside at about 23:00 BST on Monday. A force spokesperson said officers were working with "specialist teams to understand the circumstances behind this incident". Ofsted inspectors handed down damning verdicts, a headteacher left her position, and the Department for Education (DfE) made two significant interventions View 6 Images Staff on strike outside Ravensfield Primary School in January (Image: Manchester Evening News) The union blamed leadership at both schools and the multi-academy trust which runs them. But as Stephen Topping reports, Changing Lives in Collaboration (CLIC) said the allegations made 'did not reflect the day-to-day reality' at either academy and insists it is now firmly headin Stephen has been talking to former staff members like Conor Priestley, who began teaching at Lily Lane, in Moston , in September 2025 and left that December. input.evidence_text: Rudy’s Pizza Napoletana has confirmed it will be bringing its relaxed dining experience and renowned Neapolitan pizzas to Salford for the first time, with a new restaurant opening in Monton village this autumn. To celebrate, the pizzeria is giving away 3,000 pizzas on the house a The new pizzeria, located at 237-239 Monton Road , will transform the former Bennetts Furnishers store that has been vacant since 2022, with work now officially underway. The spacious venue will mark Rudy’s 41st restaurant to date Since launching in Manchester’s Ancoats in 2015, Rudy’s has grown into one of the UK’s most loved pizzerias, celebrated for its light, double fermented dough and unwavering dedication to true Neopolitan craft Testament to its authenticity, Rudy’s is the largest organisation in the world to be accredited by the Associazione Verace Pizza Napoletana (AVPN), the international body that protects and promotes traditional Neapolitan pizza making Rudy’s has also been recognised among the World’s 50 Best Pizzeria, ranking 23rd globally for 2025.
